samples.question: The picture is one chart panel with a LOGARITHMIC vertical scale. The thick dark horizontal rules are the decade rules: each thick rule stands for ten times the value of the thick rule immediately below it, and the spacing between neighbouring thick rules is the same everywhere in the panel. The thin pale horizontal rules are intermediate marks and carry no information. Standing on the bottom thick rule are four GROUPS of bars. Each group holds, from left to right, one grey bar, one coloured bar (red, green, blue or orange) and one narrow black bar. The black bars are distractors and carry no information; ignore them completely. A bar's value is read at its top edge. A group COUNTS when its coloured bar's value is more than one hundred times its own grey bar's value, which on this scale means that the coloured top stands more than two thick-rule spacings above the grey top of the same group. Two thick-rule spacings is measured on the panel itself, so it changes from picture to picture. Compare a coloured bar only with the grey bar of its own group. In every picture each coloured bar is taller than its grey partner, so height order carries no information; the tallest coloured bar need not belong to a group that counts, the bar colours and the left-to-right order of the groups carry no information, and no top sits exactly two thick-rule spacings above its partner. How many of the four groups count? Answer 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4.
